note: Plan-level evals: one failure mode per case, binary expectations, judged against the agent's described plan. The end-to-end eval that builds an app and checks that it runs is scripts/eval-create-app.sh (--agent claude|gemini|codex); e2e_requests lists the requests it was run with.

evals.prompt: A bricolo node is running. Make it show a notification with the clipboard text when I press ctrl+alt+shift+v. Describe exactly what you do, in order, with the commands you run and the files you write.
expectations: Runs `bricolo status` or lists the scripts folder before creating anything
Picks a Lua script, not a plugin, because nothing asks for sharing or a sandbox
Scaffolds with `bricolo new-script <name> --template hotkey-tool` or another listed template
Binds ctrl+alt+shift+v and calls bricolo.clipboard.get and bricolo.notify.show, checking each error
Logs a failed bind instead of raising an error
Runs `bricolo check` on the .lua file and confirms the script is running in `bricolo status`
Reads `bricolo logs --plugin <name>.lua` and reports the chord to press

evals.prompt: Make a bricolo plugin I can install on my other laptops that centers the focused window on ctrl+alt+shift+m. Describe exactly what you do, with the commands you run and the files you write.
expectations: Picks a plugin because it will be installed on other devices
Scaffolds with `bricolo new <name> --template window-tool`
Keeps the geometry in src/domain.rs with unit tests, and the window and hotkey calls in src/lib.rs
Lists log, hotkey and window in plugin.toml imports
Runs cargo test, `cargo build --target wasm32-wasip2 --release` and `bricolo check .`
Asks to approve the capabilities and the chord before `bricolo install . -y`, unless already approved
Fires the binding with `bricolo fire <plugin> <id>` and reads the plugin's log
Explains `bricolo pack` and `bricolo install github:owner/repo` for the other laptops

evals.prompt: Make a bricolo app that clicks the OK button in the dialog in front when I press ctrl+alt+shift+o.
expectations: Reads the capability list (references/capabilities.md or `bricolo wit`)
Finds no capability for mouse clicks or pressing buttons in other apps
Stops and tells the user which capability is missing instead of writing an app
Does not work around it with shell and osascript without asking the user

evals.prompt: Make me a sidecar in Python that reverses text, and a hotkey script that sends the clipboard to it on ctrl+alt+shift+r and shows the result as a toast. Describe exactly what you do, with the commands you run and the files you write.
expectations: Restates the goal in one sentence and proposes the shape (a Lua script plus a Python sidecar) without open-ended questions
Picks a free port and checks `bricolo sidecar list` (or lsof) before using it
Scaffolds with `bricolo new-sidecar <name> --template python --port <n>` and changes process() to reverse the text
Runs the sidecar's tests (python3 -m unittest) and registers it with `bricolo sidecar add`
Waits for `ready` in `bricolo sidecar list` or `bricolo status`, and checks the endpoint with curl
Scaffolds the script with `bricolo new-script <name> --template sidecar-client --port <n>` (or writes the same bricolo.http.request call) and binds ctrl+alt+shift+r
Shows the answer with bricolo.ui.toast and logs errors instead of raising them
Reports the port, the chord, `bricolo sidecar logs <name>`, and that toasts need the hub

evals.prompt: I want a bricolo plugin I can share that sends the selected text to a local LLM to fix its grammar, on ctrl+alt+shift+g. Describe the plan only.
expectations: Maps the features to capabilities and names the gaps: no selection call (keyboard cmd+c then clipboard) and the LLM (a sidecar)
Picks a WASM plugin for sharing plus a sidecar for the model, and explains why the model can't run in WASM
Lists http with `127.0.0.1:<port>` under [http] allow, plus keyboard, clipboard, hotkey and ui in imports
Asks at most a few targeted questions, such as which model, instead of an open interview
Mentions the Accessibility permission for keyboard and the model download size
Explains that bricolo pack ships the plugin but not the sidecar, which goes in the repository with its bricolo sidecar add line

e2e_requests: a Lua script that shows a notification with the clipboard text when I press ctrl+alt+shift+v
a sidecar in Python that reverses text, and a hotkey script that sends the clipboard to it on ctrl+alt+shift+r and shows the result as a toast
a sidecar in Node.js that counts the words in a text, and a Lua script that, every 60 seconds, sends the clipboard text to it and logs the count
